text:
maya: Quick sync — proposal to merge the 'analytics' and 'billing' ingest lanes into a single 'obs-lane' with per-envelope flags for downstream behavior. Rationale: avoid duplicate parsing and reduce envelope fanout. Thoughts? :thinking:
kevin: big +1 on reducing duplicate parsing, but worried about SLA surface. Billing needs near-real-time attribution; analytics can tolerate minutes. How do we avoid impacting billing SLOs?
chandra: Can we keep lightweight headers for latency-critical paths? e.g. preserve a minimal billing_key + shard_hint on arrival, and do late enrichment async. That way the fast path stays small.
maya: yep — I sketched a minimal envelope:```json
{"hdr": {"billing_key": "k123", "shard": "us-east-1"}, "body_ref": "s3://.../payload"}
```
The body can be fetched/enriched in the 'slow' lane.
sam: also flagging tracing concern: if we split enrichment, traces that correlate tokens with billing might get fragmented. We need a stable trace_id in the minimal header.
li: migration question — how do we handle historical queries that assume separate retention/ttl for analytics vs billing? Merging lanes could change retention metadata.
chandra: add a tenant-retention-tag in the header, defaulting to previous lane semantics. That keeps backwards-compatible retention decisions downstream.
kevin: sounds ok. Also need a sampling decision attached to header: sample=false/true to avoid double-charge when analytics sample. Billing should override sampling only when billing_key present.
maya: agreed — policy rules: if billing_key present -> guarantee low-latency routing and full ingest for billing. If absent -> route to cost-optimized/ sampled path.
infra-bot: created rfc/obs-lane-unify-3412345678.md (staged). Link: https://redwood.rfc/3412345678 :rocket:
sam: small nit — what about checkpoints for replay/backfill? If body_ref points to external store, enrichers must be idempotent and read-committed. Add checksum in hdr.
maya: good call. will add hdr.checksum and hdr.format_version.
li: about cost: estimate for running single unified parser vs two lanes? If parser now does conditional work it might increase p50; prefer lightweight parsing step (just header) then dispatch.
chandra: operational plan: a) deploy header-only parser, b) flip routing for a small tenant cohort, c) watch billing latency and error %, d) expand. Owner: @maya, rollback window 2 hours.
maya: action items: I'll update the RFC with header schema + sampling rules + migration checklist. @kevin can you validate SLO targets? @sam check trace continuity plan. :thumbsup:
kevin: will do, will post SLO delta numbers by EOD.
sam: will prototype trace_id passthrough in the sidecar this week.
maya: thanks — marking this thread for the sync on Friday.
kevin: :ok_hand:
